title: SaaS web app architecture
description: A typical web product: the request path from left to right, data and operations below. Click a block to see its parts

blocks.title: Clients
blocks.details: Everything that talks to the product from the outside. All clients use the same public API: the web app gets no private shortcuts.

children.title: Web app
children.details: Built and deployed to the CDN as static files. Talks to the API over HTTPS with a session cookie.

children.title: Mobile apps
children.details: Native apps with OAuth tokens. Push notifications come from the notification worker.

children.title: Partner API
children.details: Partners call the same REST API with an API key per workspace. Rate limits are stricter than for first-party clients.

blocks.title: Edge
blocks.details: The only part reachable from the internet. Everything behind it lives in a private network.

children.title: API gateway
children.details:
- Routes `/api/*` to the services
- Rate limits per user and per API key
- Rejects requests without a valid session or token, so services can trust the caller

children.title: CDN
children.details: Serves the web app and public images. Cache keys include the build hash, so a deploy never serves stale code.

children.title: Firewall
children.details: Blocks known attack patterns and abusive bots before they reach the gateway.

blocks.title: Application
blocks.details: Stateless services behind the gateway, scaled horizontally, plus the workers that run anything slow or retryable. They keep no data of their own: state lives in the data layer.

children.title: Billing
children.details: Handles Stripe webhooks and keeps the current plan of each workspace. The core API asks it for limits.

children.title: Core API
children.details: The main REST API. Writes go to PostgreSQL in a transaction; every change also publishes an event for the workers.

children.title: Auth
children.details: OpenID Connect with Google and GitHub, email magic links, sessions in Redis. Issues the tokens the gateway checks.

children.title: Search
children.details: Reads from the search index; the index is filled by a worker from core API events.

children.title: Background jobs
children.description: Queue, workers, scheduler: anything slow or retryable
children.details: Anything slow or retryable runs here, never inside a request. The services publish events to the queue.

children.title: Queue
children.details: Durable queue with retries and a dead-letter queue for jobs that keep failing.

children.title: Workers
children.details:
- Sends emails and push notifications
- Builds CSV and PDF exports
- Updates the search index

children.title: Scheduler
children.details: Cleans up expired sessions, sends digests, reconciles billing with Stripe.

blocks.title: Operations
blocks.description: Logs, metrics, alerts and deploys for every layer
blocks.details: Watches every layer above. Not on the request path, so it is not linked to them.

children.title: Observability
children.details: Structured logs, metrics with alerts on error rate and latency, distributed traces across the gateway and services.

children.title: CI/CD
children.details: Every merge to main runs tests, builds images and deploys to staging; production deploys are one click.

children.title: Infrastructure as code
children.details: Networks, databases and services are described in code and reviewed like any other change.

blocks.title: Data
blocks.details: The only stateful layer. Backed up nightly; the database has a hot replica for reads and failover.

children.title: PostgreSQL
children.details: Source of truth for workspaces, projects, users and billing state. Point-in-time recovery for 14 days.

children.title: Redis
children.details: Short-lived data only: losing it logs users out, nothing more.

children.title: Object storage
children.details: S3-compatible bucket. Files are served through signed URLs that expire after an hour.

children.title: Search index
children.details: Can be dropped and rebuilt from PostgreSQL at any time.
